summary: Copies the first input POP geometry and runs GLSL compute shaders for each copy. Copy count comes from Number of Copies when no template POP is connected, or from the template input point count when the second input is connected; point shaders are required while vertex and primitive shaders can use default topology-copy behavior.

common_gotchas: A valid point compute shader is required; vertex and primitive compute shaders can stay on the default method when only topology and attributes need to be copied.
When a template input is connected, Number of Copies is ignored and one copy is created for each template point.
Custom vertex shaders that change or rely on topology should call TDUpdateTopology(); the default vertex shader performs topology and vertex attribute copy behavior.
Custom primitive shaders for line strips or primitive groups should use TDUpdateLineStripsInfo() and TDUpdatePrimGroups() when preserving those metadata buffers.
The GLSL Copy POP has only source and template inputs; attributes from any other POP must be exposed through POP Buffers and read with TDBuffer().
Use TDCopyIndex() for the current copy and TDInputIndex() for the source point, vertex, or primitive that the current output element corresponds to.
Template attributes use TDTemplate_AttribName() and cTDTemplateArraySize_Attrib constants; source input array attributes use cTDArraySize_Attrib.
Output attributes are written through AttribName[] arrays, so list every point, vertex, or primitive attribute to modify in the matching Output Attributes parameter.
Line-strip custom code must preserve primitive restart handling with cTDPrimIndexRestart when rebuilding index data.
Array uniforms can be backed by texture buffers; keep array type and CHOP channel layout aligned with the GLSL declaration.
